## Why this session {.smaller}

- If you already write R code, you know *what* a package is.
- To share your code, you need to know *how* to make a package.
- To make your package robust, you need to learn how to debug, test, and publish it.
- Format: **watch-along**. Repo + slides shared afterward.
- We work one small package end-to-end: **framecheck** (data validation).

## The big picture {.smaller}

Steps to update code in a package:

::: {.r-fit-text}
**Make a change → Prove it's correct → Ship it safely**
:::

| Step | What it means | Today's segments |
|---|---|---|
| Make a change | write code, manage deps | **Build** (1–2) |
| Prove it's correct | find & lock down behavior | **Debug** + **Test** (3–4) |
| Ship it safely | release to your users | **Publish** (5) |

These steps spin the **development loop** we repeat:

> edit code → `load_all()` → `document()` → `test()` → `check()`

# 1 · Orientation & internals {background-color="#1b4965"}

## The tooling {.smaller}

R packages used to build packages:

- **devtools**: the Swiss Army knife for package development
- **usethis**: automates common package development tasks
- **roxygen2**: write documentation inline with code, generate help files
- **testthat**: framework for writing and running tests

## Anatomy of a package {.smaller}

- **DESCRIPTION** — metadata (what the package does, author, version, dependencies)
- **NAMESPACE** — functions available to the users (generated automatically from roxygen2)
- **R/** — your functions (the code)
- **man/** — the help files (generated automatically from roxygen2)
- **tests/** — test files to validate the behavior of your code (using testthat)

## The development loop {.smaller}

Edit the code → `load_all()` → try it out → `document()` → `test()` → `check()`

* `load_all()` simulates installing the package without actually installing it, so you can test changes quickly.
* `document()` regenerates the documentation and NAMESPACE based on your code comments.
* `test()` runs your tests to check your code works as expected.
* `check()` runs a comprehensive set of checks to ensure the architecture of your package is correct (and optionally meets CRAN standards).

## Positron makes this easier {.smaller}

- Build / package actions + command palette (no typing `load_all`)
- Integrated R console + terminal
- Jump-to-definition across the package


# 2 · Building {background-color="#1b4965"}

## Dependency hygiene {.smaller}

- use `load_all()` (and not `install()` during development)
- `usethis::use_package()` to declare dependencies
- **Imports** (needed at run time) vs **Suggests** (tests/examples)
- `::` and `@importFrom` for explicit namespace management

## roxygen2 round-trip {.smaller}

- Edit the function documentation → `document()` → `man/` + `NAMESPACE` regenerate.
- Preview help files with `?my_function` or `help("my_function")`
- use `@export` to make a function available to users

*Demo:* fix framecheck's missing `cli` declaration, re-document, re-check.

# 3 · Debugging {background-color="#5fa8d3"}

## The bug {.smaller}

`framecheck` reports an **all-NA column as PASSING** a range check.
A real-world "my data was empty but everything looked green" failure.

## Escalation ladder {.smaller}

- `traceback()` to see where the error occurred
- `print`/`cli` leave breadcrumbs by making your function tell you where it is at
- `debug()` / `debugonce()` to step through a function line by line on the next call
- `browser()` interactive breakpoint so you can inspect the environment at that moment
- `options(error = recover)` to drop into the environment of any error, even in tests

## Positron's debugger (the centerpiece) {.smaller}

- Set **breakpoints in the gutter**
- Step over / into / out
- Inspect the **call stack + variables** mid-execution
- Conditional breakpoints; evaluate in the debug console

## Discipline {.smaller}

> A bug you fix without a test will come back.

# 4 · Testing {background-color="#5fa8d3"}

## testthat {.smaller}

- `test_that()` uses expectations (`expect_true`, `expect_equal`, `expect_error`, ... )
- Turn the bug into a **regression test** first — watch it fail, then fix
- Cover what breaks: `NA`, empty, wrong type
- **Snapshot tests** for cli/message output
- `withr` for clean setup/teardown

## Positron makes this easier {.smaller}

- Test Explorer: run/filter individual tests, inline pass/fail
- Run tests on save
- `devtools::check()` — the all-in-one gate

# 5 · Publishing: CI/CD + PPM {background-color="#1b4965"}

## Checks gate the merge {.smaller}

- `usethis::use_github_action("check-standard")`
- r-lib actions: matrix across OS × R versions
- Required status checks on PRs — **nobody merges red**

## PPM: how it's wired up {.smaller}

Three building blocks: **source** → **repository** → **URL**

```bash
# 1. A source = where packages come from (git OR local)
rspm create source --name=internal-src --type=git   # or --type=local
# 2. A repository = a served collection
rspm create repo   --name=internal
# 3. Subscribe the repo to the source
rspm subscribe --repo=internal --source=internal-src
```

Users then point R at the repo URL:

```r
options(repos = c(INTERNAL = "https://ppm.example.com/internal/latest"))
install.packages("framecheck")
```

## Two ways to publish to PPM {.smaller}

| | **Push** — local source | **Pull** — git source |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | CI calls PPM **after checks pass** | PPM **polls** the repo |
| Mechanism | `R CMD build` → upload `.tar.gz` via `rspm add` / PPM API | `git-builder` builds from a branch/tag |
| Who builds | **CI** (exact checked artifact is served) | **PPM** (rebuilds from source) |
| Gate | only build+upload when green | only **merge/tag** when green |
| Needs | CI → PPM credentials | PPM build env has the deps |

- **Push** = imperative, green checks. **Pull** = declarative, git is the trigger.
- Either way, **successful checks are the gate**

## Staging → production {.smaller}

The same split works with **either** path:

| Stage | Git path: builder watches | Push path: CI publishes to | Audience |
|---|---|---|---|
| **staging** | the `main` **branch** | a `dev` local source | early adopters |
| **production** | git **tags** (`v0.1.0`) | a `prod` local source | everyone |

- A tag (or a green release build) = the promotion trigger
- Snapshots / repository versioning for reproducibility

## Versioning {.smaller}

- Bump in DESCRIPTION: `usethis::use_version()`
- Dev vs release: `0.1.0.9000` vs `0.1.0`
- Tag the release → prod builder picks it up

## CRAN (for the packages that go public) {.smaller}

- Same `R CMD check` discipline **is** the CRAN bar
- `R CMD check --as-cran`, `urlchecker::url_check()`
- CRAN policies + `cran-comments.md` — not a full submission today

## The Python parallel {.smaller}

Same discipline, different tools:

| R | Python |
|---|---|
| devtools / usethis | uv / hatch / setuptools |
| roxygen2 | docstrings + Sphinx |
| testthat | pytest |
| `R CMD check` | ruff + `python -m build` |
| PPM `git` source | PPM `git-python` source |
| CRAN | PyPI |

## Takeaways {.smaller}

- Same arc, every time: **make a change → prove it's correct → ship it safely**
- The dev loop is muscle memory: `load_all → document → test → check`
- Every fix earns a test
- For internal packages, CI gates the merge; tags promote to prod via PPM
- These are habits that work in every programming language: write the test, run the check, gate the merge
